definition: σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (σάρξ)  (seel. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7) = Lat. carnalis, i.e.  __(a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Rom.15:27, 1Co.9:11;  __(b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, 1Pe., 133): 1Co.3:3, 2Co.1:12 10:4, 1Pe.2:11.† SYN.: σάρκινος (which see), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ LXXi, LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on Rom.7:14  (AS)
